c.tagline: Ancient West Bank city built around the revered Cave of the Patriarchs and a centuries-old stone souq.

taxi.fareNote: Shared 'service' taxis run fixed routes for a set per-person fare; private taxis should have the price agreed before departure.

emergency.note: Numbers reach Palestinian Civil Police and the Palestine Red Crescent Society. Hebron is administratively split into H1 (Palestinian Authority control) and H2 (Israeli military control) under the 1997 Hebron Protocol; movement through the Old City/H2 involves Israeli military checkpoints, and visitors should check current conditions before traveling, especially around the Old City and Ibrahimi Mosque area.

hood_landmark.Old City: Cave of the Patriarchs / Ibrahimi Mosque

avoid.reason: Avoid the H2 zone around Shuhada Street and the checkpoints near the Ibrahimi Mosque during periods of unrest, when clashes can erupt with little warning.
Exercise extra care near military checkpoints and settler-Palestinian friction points in the Old City, especially on Fridays after prayers when protests are more likely.

hood_desc: The historic walled core containing the Ibrahimi Mosque/Cave of the Patriarchs, the centuries-old covered souq, and Mamluk-era stone architecture; part of this district (H2) is under Israeli military control with checkpoints and some closed streets.
A busy commercial spine south of the Old City with everyday shops, cafes, and street vendors popular with local Hebronites.
Home to Hebron's traditional glassblowing and ceramics workshops, a craft the city has practiced for centuries; visitors can watch artisans at work and buy directly from factory shops.
A residential and educational district anchored by Hebron University, with a younger, more modern feel than the Old City.
A dense commercial district around Bab al-Zawiya, one of the city's main market and transit hubs, with produce stalls, textiles, and shared-taxi stands.

water.note: Stick to bottled water; supply and quality can be inconsistent.

transit.pay: Cash (shekels) paid directly to the driver
transit.map: No official transit map; ask your hotel or locals for current shared-taxi routes
transit.note: No formal public transit system or map; shared 'service' taxis and minibuses connect Hebron to Bethlehem, Ramallah, and other West Bank towns. Access to and movement within the Old City/H2 area can be affected by Israeli military checkpoints.

bus: Shared 'service' taxis and buses connect to Bethlehem and onward to Jerusalem/Ramallah checkpoints

tip.r: Tipping is uncommon; small gratuities are appreciated at restaurants but not required.
